title.en: Who do we serve, and how do they see us?
title.zh: 我们服务谁，他们怎么看我们？

description.en: Segmentation with five tests, targeting, and positioning on a map in the customer’s mind, with Who Gives a Crap and Lipton.
description.zh: 用五项检验做细分、选目标，并在顾客心智的地图上做定位，案例是 Who Gives a Crap 和 Lipton。

name.en: Explaining and applying segmentation, targeting and positioning
name.zh: 解释并应用细分、目标市场与定位

description.en: segmentation means splitting by age and gender
description.zh: 细分就是按年龄和性别切分

description.en: positioning is what the firm says about itself
description.zh: 定位就是企业怎么说自己

title.en: One aisle, more than one buyer
title.zh: 一条货架，不止一种买家

text.en: Who Gives a Crap sells toilet paper in a category that one supermarket own-brand roll could fill for every home. Yet the company has found buyers who pay for something extra. If every buyer wanted the same thing, a firm could sell one thing to all. They do not.
text.zh: Who Gives a Crap 卖卷纸，而这个品类里一款超市自有品牌就能满足所有家庭。可是这家公司找到了愿意为“额外的东西”付钱的买家。如果所有买家想要的都一样，企业只卖一种东西就行。事实并非如此。

text.en: So a firm has to answer three questions in order: **which groups differ, which of them will we serve, and what place do we want in their minds?**
text.zh: 所以企业要按顺序回答三个问题：**哪些群体不同、我们服务哪些、想在他们心里占什么位置？**

prompt.en: A firm splits its market into twenty tiny segments and builds an offer for each. What is most likely?
prompt.zh: 一家企业把市场切成二十个很小的细分，并为每个做一套方案。最可能的结果是什么？

label.en: Each offer fits its group better, but cost goes up and some segments are too small to pay
label.zh: 每套方案更贴合各自的群体，但成本上升，有些细分太小养不活

label.en: Profit rises with every extra segment
label.zh: 每多一个细分利润就多一点

feedback.en: Each segment adds cost. There is a point past which extra fit does not pay.
feedback.zh: 每个细分都增加成本。超过某个点后，多出来的贴合度不值回成本。

label.en: Nothing changes, because customers ignore segments
label.zh: 没有变化，因为顾客不在乎细分

feedback.en: They do not ignore an offer that fits them, which is why segmenting works at all.
feedback.zh: 对贴合自己的方案，顾客不会无视，细分才有意义。

label.en: Costs fall because each offer is simpler
label.zh: 成本下降，因为每套方案更简单

feedback.en: Twenty offers are more complex, not simpler.
feedback.zh: 二十套方案更复杂，不是更简单。

explain.en: That tension is the **efficiency versus effectiveness trade-off**: mass marketing is efficient but fits no one well; one-to-one marketing fits perfectly but costs a lot. Move the dial to see it.
explain.zh: 这个张力就是**效率与效果的取舍**：大众营销效率高但谁都不太贴合；一对一营销最贴合但成本很高。动一动转盘看看。

text.en: Serving more segments fits each group better and costs more to run.
text.zh: 服务的细分越多，对每组越贴合，运营也越贵。

alt.en: A dial for the number of segments; two curves show how well the offers fit and what they cost to run.
alt.zh: 用于调节细分数量的转盘；两条曲线显示方案的贴合度和运营成本。

label.en: How well offers fit buyers (0 to 100)
label.zh: 方案对买家的贴合度（0 到 100）

text.en: **One segment** is mass marketing: cheap, but the offer fits nobody closely.
text.zh: **一个细分**就是大众营销：便宜，但方案对谁都不够贴合。

text.en: **Many segments** is micromarketing: each offer fits, but cost climbs faster than fit.
text.zh: **很多细分**就是微观营销：每套方案都贴合，但成本爬升得比贴合度快。

text.en: **In between**: fit has gained most of its value and cost has not run away. Where exactly depends on the firm’s own costs.
text.zh: **中间地带**：贴合度已经拿到大部分收益，成本还没失控。具体在哪，取决于企业自己的成本。

caption.en: The two curves are drawn for this lesson to show the shape of the trade-off; they are not measured on any company.
caption.zh: 两条曲线是为说明取舍的形状画的，不是任何公司的实测数据。

title.zh: 这是一个真正的细分市场吗？

text.en: A group of buyers is only worth treating as a segment if it passes five tests (Mooi and Sarstedt). Each of these groups fails one. Say which.
text.zh: 一群买家只有通过五项检验（Mooi 和 Sarstedt），才值得当作一个细分市场。下面每个群体都挂在其中一项上。

alt.en: Five candidate segments, each failing one test: actionable, measurable, accessible, differentiable, substantial.
alt.zh: 五个候选细分，各自不通过一项检验：可行动、可测量、可触达、反应有差别、规模足够。

text.en: “People who quietly care about sanitation”, but no data or survey can tell us who they are (an illustration)
text.zh: “默默关心卫生问题的人”，但没有任何数据或调查能告诉我们他们是谁（举例）

why.en: If you cannot find out its size, purchasing power or characteristics, you cannot measure it.
why.zh: 如果查不出它的规模、购买力和特征，就无法测量。

text.en: Households in a remote area no courier will deliver to (an illustration)
text.zh: 没有快递愿意送到的偏远地区家庭（举例）

why.en: You cannot reach or serve them.
why.zh: 你触达不到、也服务不了他们。

text.en: A group of 40 buyers in the whole country (an illustration)
text.zh: 全国只有 40 个买家的群体（举例）

why.en: Not large or profitable enough to justify a separate offer.
why.zh: 不够大、不够赚钱，不值得单独做一套方案。

text.en: A group who react to our price promotions and our brand message exactly like everyone else (an illustration)
text.zh: 对我们的价格促销和品牌信息的反应，和其他人完全一样的一群人（举例）

why.en: If it does not respond differently to the marketing mix, it is not worth treating as a separate segment.
why.zh: 如果它对营销组合的反应没有差别，就不值得当作单独的细分市场。

text.en: A group we are not able to attract or convince to buy with any offer we can make (an illustration)
text.zh: 我们拿得出的任何方案都吸引不了、说服不了购买的一群人（举例）

why.en: A segment is useful only if you can act on it: attract and win customers.
why.zh: 细分市场只有在你能采取行动时才有用：吸引并赢得顾客。

done.en: The five tests: **Actionable** (can we attract and make them buy?), **Measurable** (size, purchasing power, characteristics?), **Accessible** (can we reach and serve them?), **Differentiable** (do they respond differently to the marketing mix?), **Substantial** (large and profitable enough?).
done.zh: 五项检验：**可行动**（能吸引并让他们购买吗？）、**可测量**（规模、购买力、特征？）、**可触达**（能触达并服务吗？）、**反应有差别**（对营销组合反应不同吗？）、**规模足够**（够大够赚钱吗？）。

title.en: Where do they sit in a customer’s mind?
title.zh: 它们在顾客心里坐在哪？

text.en: A **perceptual map** places brands as customers see them. These placements are the course’s readings, to show how it works; a real map would come from asking customers.
text.zh: **感知图**把品牌放在顾客眼里的位置上。这些放置是本课程的解读，用来演示方法；真正的图要靠问顾客得出。

alt.en: Six products to place on a price by specialness map.
alt.zh: 六个产品，放到“价格与特别程度”的感知图上。

label.en: Who Gives a Crap toilet paper
label.zh: Who Gives a Crap 卷纸

why.en: Priced at or above budget brands, and it stands out through its giving and its paper-wrapped, bulk, direct delivery.
why.zh: 定价不低于平价品牌，靠捐赠和纸包装、批量直送而突出。

why.en: Built to be the low-price default.
why.zh: 以低价默认选项为目标。

why.en: Pays more for softness but is not different in what it stands for.
why.zh: 为柔软度付更多钱，但在“代表什么”上并不特别。

label.en: A small shop’s loose-leaf specialty tea
Lipton tea bags as an everyday supermarket tea
label.zh: Lipton 茶包，作为超市日常茶饮

why.en: A mass-market everyday tea: cheap and familiar rather than special. This is a reading from what any shopper sees.
why.zh: 大众日常茶：便宜、熟悉而不特别。这是从任何购物者都看得到的东西得出的解读。

label.en: A cheap tea bag in a plain pack

done.en: A map has only the two dimensions you choose, so the choice matters: **they come from what buyers use to decide** (found with multidimensional scaling of customer data), not from guesses. A gap in the map is a position nobody holds; a crowded corner is a fight.
done.zh: 感知图只有你选的两个维度，所以选择很重要：**维度来自买家做决定时用的标准**（用顾客数据做多维尺度分析得到），不是猜的。图上的空缺是没人占的位置；挤满的角落就是一场混战。

title.en: The framework, as the marker wants it

text.en: **Market segmentation** (Smith, 1956) is viewing one varied market as a smaller number of similar markets, because buyers differ in preferences, desires and attitudes. Then **targeting** selects one or more segments to enter, and **positioning** establishes, communicates and delivers the right benefit for each target segment: that is where the value proposition comes from (next lesson).
text.zh: **市场细分**（Smith，1956）是把一个差异很大的市场看作少数几个内部相似的市场，因为买家的偏好、愿望和态度不同。**目标市场选择**挑出一个或几个细分去进入；**定位**为每个目标细分确立、沟通并交付恰当的利益点：价值主张由此而来（下一课）。

rows.en: user status, usage frequency, store or brand loyalty
rows.zh: 用户状态、使用频率、门店/品牌忠诚度
心理特征、价值观、个性、生活方式

rows.en: benefits, perceptions, elasticities, attributes, preferences, intentions, conjoint part-worths
rows.zh: 利益、认知、弹性、属性、偏好、意向、联合分析分值

text.en: Segmenting is a trade-off between **efficiency** (one mass market) and **effectiveness** (one-to-one). **Tracking and repositioning**: a campaign can aim to shift perceptions (a car maker courting younger drivers with edgier adverts), and the same map is used to see if it worked.
text.zh: 细分是**效率**（一个大众市场）与**效果**（一对一）之间的取舍。**追踪与重新定位**：一次营销活动可以以改变认知为目标（汽车厂商用更前卫的广告争取年轻车主），同一张图可用来检验是否奏效。

prompt.en: Take **Lipton tea bags** in Australia. Nothing about its Australian segments is verified, so reason openly. Write four sentences: name **one** segment by a basis from the table, say whether it passes at least two of the five tests and why, and where you would put Lipton on a price by specialness map.
prompt.zh: 以澳大利亚的 **Lipton 茶包**为例。它在澳大利亚的细分情况没有核实，所以要公开推理。写四句话：用表里的一种依据说出**一个**细分，说它是否通过五项检验中至少两项以及原因，并说你把 Lipton 放在价格与特别程度的图上哪里。

key_points.en: Names a segment by a clear basis (for example usage occasion, a behavioural basis)
key_points.zh: 用清晰的依据命名一个细分（如使用场合，一种行为依据）

key_points.en: Tests it against at least two of the five tests with a reason each
key_points.zh: 用五项检验中至少两项各给理由

key_points.en: Places Lipton on the map and says why, flagged as a reading
key_points.zh: 把 Lipton 放在图上并说明原因，标为解读
不编造澳大利亚的数字

model_answer.en: One segment is people who want a quick everyday cup at home, defined by usage occasion. It is measurable and accessible, because supermarkets sell tea to nearly every household, and substantial because tea is bought widely. On the map I would place Lipton in lower price and less special, because a familiar tea bag on a supermarket shelf competes as an everyday default; this is my reading from what shoppers see, and I have no Australian figures. The implication is that its position is held by familiarity and price, so a premium move would need a different segment.
model_answer.zh: 一个细分是想在家快速泡一杯日常茶的人，按使用场合定义。它可测量、可触达，因为超市把茶卖给几乎每个家庭；规模足够，因为茶被广泛购买。在图上我会把 Lipton 放在价格较低、不特别的位置，因为超市货架上熟悉的茶包是以日常默认选项的身份竞争的；这是我从购物者看得见的东西得出的解读，我没有澳大利亚的数字。含义是它的位置靠熟悉和价格守住，所以要往高端走就需要换一个细分。

explain.en: Reason openly and say it is a reading.
explain.zh: 公开推理，并说明这是解读。

prompt.en: A firm’s slogan says “we are the caring brand”. Is that its positioning?
prompt.zh: 一家企业的口号是“我们是有爱心的品牌”。这就是它的定位吗？

label.en: No: positioning is the place customers actually give the brand in their minds, which a map can show
label.zh: 不是：定位是顾客在心里实际给品牌的位置，可以用感知图看出来

label.en: Yes: what a firm says is its position
label.zh: 是：企业怎么说，位置就是什么

feedback.en: What the firm says is a message; customers decide the position.
feedback.zh: 企业说的是信息；位置由顾客决定。

label.en: Yes, if it is repeated enough

feedback.en: Repetition can shift a position, and the map is how you check.
feedback.zh: 重复可以改变位置，用感知图来检验。

explain.en: Position is in the customer’s mind.

prompt.en: From lesson 4: Porter, Ansoff and the value disciplines answer which questions?
prompt.zh: 来自第 4 课：Porter、Ansoff 和价值准则分别回答什么问题？

label.en: How to compete; where to grow; what to excel at
label.zh: 怎么竞争；往哪增长；擅长什么

prompt.en: From lesson 1: which type of value does a donation-led brand mostly offer?
prompt.zh: 来自第 1 课：以捐赠为特色的品牌主要提供哪类价值？

feedback.en: It usually asks for more, not less.
feedback.zh: 它通常要求更多付出，而不是更少。

explain.en: It carries meaning for the buyer.

prompt.en:
Question. (a) Explain segmentation, targeting and positioning. (b) Apply them to Who Gives a Crap in Australia. (c) Make two recommendations.

Explain (5 marks). Exceeds: precise, thorough, clear, with the right terms. Meets: accurate, key points present, a little shallow.

Write the **Explain** part.
prompt.zh:
题目。(a) 解释细分、目标市场选择和定位。(b) 把它们应用到澳大利亚的 Who Gives a Crap。(c) 给出两条建议。

解释（5 分）。优秀：精确、完整、清楚，用对术语。达标：准确、要点齐全，但深度略浅。

写**解释**部分。

key_points.en: Segmentation: viewing a market as groups with different needs, tested for actionable, measurable, accessible, differentiable, substantial
key_points.zh: 细分：把市场看作需求不同的群体，用可行动、可测量、可触达、有差别、规模足够检验

key_points.en: Targeting: choosing which segments to enter
key_points.zh: 目标市场选择：选择进入哪些细分

key_points.en: Positioning: the benefit established and communicated for each target segment, and place in customers’ minds
key_points.zh: 定位：为每个目标细分确立和沟通的利益，以及在顾客心智中的位置

model_answer.en: Segmentation (Smith, 1956) divides a varied market into groups with similar needs. A useful segment is actionable, measurable, accessible, differentiable and substantial. Targeting selects the segments the firm will serve; positioning establishes and communicates the benefit it offers each target, so that customers hold a distinct place for the brand in their minds, often shown on a perceptual map. The choice of how many segments trades efficiency, as in mass marketing, against effectiveness, as in micromarketing.
model_answer.zh: 细分（Smith，1956）把差异很大的市场分成需求相似的群体。有用的细分要可行动、可测量、可触达、反应有差别、规模足够。目标市场选择决定企业服务哪些细分；定位则为每个目标确立并沟通所提供的利益，使顾客在心里给品牌一个独特的位置，常用感知图表示。细分多少，是在大众营销式的效率和微观营销式的效果之间取舍。

explain.en: Compare with the key points and the model answer. A scoring answer says the thing, shows it on this company, and stops.
explain.zh: 对照要点和参考答案。拿分的答案：把概念说准，落到这家公司上，然后收住。

prompt.en:
Question. (a) Explain segmentation, targeting and positioning. (b) Apply them to Who Gives a Crap in Australia. (c) Make two recommendations.

Apply (10 marks). Exceeds: this company, rigorous cause and effect, evidence from the case. Meets: correct and logical, connections could go deeper.

Write the **Apply** part.
prompt.zh:
题目。(a) 解释细分、目标市场选择和定位。(b) 把它们应用到澳大利亚的 Who Gives a Crap。(c) 给出两条建议。

应用（10 分）。优秀：针对这家公司，因果分析严密，有案例证据。达标：应用正确、逻辑通顺，但联系还可以更深。

写**应用**部分。

key_points.en: Identifies a target segment for Who Gives a Crap with a clear basis (values, attitude)
key_points.zh: 为 Who Gives a Crap 指出一个目标细分及其依据（价值观、态度）

key_points.en: Uses true facts: 50% of profits donated, B Corp, direct to consumer online, priced at or above budget brands, paper-wrapped rolls
key_points.zh: 用真实事实：50% 利润捐赠、B Corp、线上直销、定价不低于平价品牌、纸包装

key_points.en: Tests the segment on the five tests with reasons
key_points.zh: 用五项检验检验该细分，并给理由

key_points.en: Positions the brand against competitors and explains the effect on price and channel
key_points.zh: 对照竞争对手定位品牌，并说明对价格和渠道的影响

model_answer.en: Who Gives a Crap targets values-led households, a segment defined by attitude rather than demographics. It is actionable, because its giving, B Corp status and paper-wrapped rolls speak to that attitude; accessible, because it sells online direct to consumers; and differentiable, because these buyers respond to the cause where others respond to price. Measurability is its weak test, since attitudes are inferred, and size is limited because the price is at or above budget brands. Its position is therefore high on purpose and not low on price, far from supermarket own-brand rolls. That position explains the direct channel, since it lets the company tell its story without a retailer, and the premium price, which the segment accepts.
model_answer.zh: Who Gives a Crap 瞄准以价值观为导向的家庭，这个细分按态度而不是人口特征定义。它可行动，因为捐赠、B Corp 身份和纸包装直接对应这种态度；可触达，因为它在线直接卖给消费者；反应有差别，因为这些买家为理念买单，而别人只看价格。可测量性是它的弱项，因为态度是推断出来的；规模受限，因为价格不低于平价品牌。所以它的位置是“公益含量高、价格不低”，远离超市自有品牌卷纸。这个位置解释了它的直销渠道，因为这让公司不经零售商也能讲自己的故事；也解释了溢价，因为这个细分接受溢价。

explain.en: Compare with the key points and the model answer. A scoring answer says the thing, shows it on this company, and stops.
explain.zh: 对照要点和参考答案。拿分的答案：把概念说准，落到这家公司上，然后收住。

prompt.en:
Question. (a) Explain segmentation, targeting and positioning. (b) Apply them to Who Gives a Crap in Australia. (c) Make two recommendations.

Recommend (5 marks). Exceeds: exactly two, realistic, strategic, actionable, each following from your analysis, with a risk named. Meets: sound but thin on how.

Write the **Recommend** part: exactly two.
prompt.zh:
题目。(a) 解释细分、目标市场选择和定位。(b) 把它们应用到澳大利亚的 Who Gives a Crap。(c) 给出两条建议。

建议（5 分）。优秀：恰好两条，现实、有战略性、可执行，都从你的分析里推出来，并点出风险。达标：合理，但“怎么做”偏薄。

写**建议**部分：恰好两条。

key_points.zh: 恰好两条，从分析里推出

model_answer.en: First, measure the segment: add a short question at checkout about why customers chose the brand, so attitudes become data. This fixes the weakest test; the risk is survey fatigue, so keep it to one question. Second, test a smaller trial pack aimed at price-conscious but sympathetic shoppers to see if a second segment passes the tests. The risk is diluting the premium position, so keep the trial pack clearly the same brand with the same giving.
model_answer.zh: 第一，把这个细分测量出来：在结账时加一个简短问题，问顾客为何选择这个品牌，让态度变成数据。这补上最弱的一项检验；风险是问卷疲劳，所以只问一个问题。第二，面向在乎价格但认同理念的购物者测试更小的试用装，看第二个细分能否通过检验。风险是稀释高端定位，所以试用装要明确是同一品牌、同样捐赠。

explain.en: Compare with the key points and the model answer. A scoring answer says the thing, shows it on this company, and stops.
explain.zh: 对照要点和参考答案。拿分的答案：把概念说准，落到这家公司上，然后收住。
